questions.q: Why does checking every VM in a subscription require a loop rather than one Get-AzVM command per VM?
options: Because retyping the same command once per VM doesn't scale as the number of VMs grows
Because Get-AzVM can only ever return exactly one VM at a time
Because loops are required syntax in every PowerShell script, regardless of the task
Because Stop-AzVM cannot accept a ResourceGroupName parameter
questions.explain: Get-AzVM already returns every VM in a subscription as a collection; a loop runs the same logic once per item in that collection instead of requiring one command per VM.

questions.q: In foreach ($vm in $vms) { ... }, what does $vm represent?
options: The current VM object for that pass through the loop
The total count of VMs in the $vms collection
A string containing the subscription ID
The name of the loop itself
questions.explain: Each time through the loop, $vm holds the next VM object from the $vms collection, with the same properties any single Get-AzVM result has.

questions.q: What does Get-AzVM -Status add to each returned VM object?
options: A PowerState property, such as "VM running" or "VM stopped"
A new resource group that the VM is moved into
A list of every VM in every other subscription
A permanent price-tier change
questions.explain: The -Status flag populates a PowerState property on each VM object, used in this lesson's worked example to build a power-state report.

questions.q: In Get-AzVM | Where-Object { $_.Tags["Environment"] -eq "Dev" } | ForEach-Object { ... }, what does Where-Object do?
options: Filters the VM collection down to only the tagged Dev VMs before the loop runs
Deletes every VM that is not tagged Dev
Renames every VM's resource group to "Dev"
Has no effect when placed before ForEach-Object
questions.explain: Where-Object narrows the pipeline to just the VMs whose Environment tag equals Dev, and only those flow into the ForEach-Object loop afterward.

questions.q: What does the -NoWait parameter do when passed to Stop-AzVM inside a loop over multiple VMs?
options: Submits each stop request without waiting for the previous one to finish before starting the next
Cancels the stop operation entirely
Forces the script to pause for user confirmation on every VM
Prevents Stop-AzVM from running more than once
questions.explain: -NoWait lets the loop submit all the stop requests quickly, rather than blocking on each VM's shutdown before moving to the next one.
